the psychological processes of the victim-to- patient process.

(1) understanding the nature of the victim-to patient process; (2) the psychological processes of women who are victims of violence; and (3) the relationship between the victim-to-patients process and mental disorders in women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the victim-to-patients process is a dynamic and complex one, which can be understood and explained by the interaction of the individual, social and environmental factors.

the mental health of women victims of violence is a function of the interaction between the psychological and biological processes, the nature of the violence, the individual’s psychological and biological makeup and her coping skills.
the psychological processes of women are not the cause of the violence but are the result of the violence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the victim of violence, particularly the victim of sexual violence, is a person who has been subjected to a traumatic event.
women’s mental health issues are often the result of the victimization process.
women who have been victims of violence are at risk of becoming patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the victim to patient process is not a simple one.
the mental health of women who are victimized is often compromised by their victimization.
the mental health system needs to do a much better job in helping victims cope with their experiences and recover from the trauma of sexual violence.
